findings.finding: The plan's re-export rationale rests on a false premise: it states the relocated names are 'plain from ... import consumers (not monkeypatch targets)', but `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` is monkeypatched at the string target `rebar._commands.compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` in at least 5 test call sites (tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py:46 and test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py:97,131,189,229). The refactor is only safe because the internal fsck consumers (fsck.py:181, fsck_repair.py:266) use function-local `from ... import` that re-reads the patched attribute — and because a plain re-export creates a real module attribute on compact.py that monkeypatch can still replace. The plan neither states this actual load-bearing condition nor lists those monkeypatch tests in its verification set, so the monkeypatch-survival property goes unverified.
findings.location: Plan section 'Preserve public + test import paths via re-export (G1G2)' — sentence 'These are plain from ... import consumers (not monkeypatch targets)'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 'not monkeypatch targets' sentence with: 'rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log is a monkeypatch target (patched via the string rebar._commands.compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log); the re-export MUST bind it as a real module attribute on compact.py (via `from .compact_rebuild import rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`) so the attribute stays patchable, and fsck.py/fsck_repair.py retain their function-local imports so they re-read the patched value. Add tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair.py and _heldout.py to Verification.'
